To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have observed the semi electronic decay of charm mesons in dAu collisions at RHIC, and we have measured the single electron spectra for the first time in this collision system at RHIC.
the single electrons from the semi electronic decays of heavy flavor meson have been observed for the first time in d+Au at RHIC.

we have measured the single electron spectra in d+Au and p+p collisions at s N = 200 and s N = 62 GeV and found that the spectra are consistent with a simple convolution of the p+p spectra with the number of binary nucleon-nucleon collisions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of heavy flavor decay electron production in d+Au and p+p collisions at RHIC energies.
the measurement of single electron spectra in d+Au and Au+Au at RHIC.
the study of heavy flavor meson production in p+p and d+Au collisions at 200 GeV.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the single electron spectrum in d+Au is not significantly modified from the p+p case and the suppression in the Au+Au case can be attributed to the hot nuclear matter.
the semi-leptonic decays of heavy flavor meson in d+Au are not suppressed compared with the scaled p+p data, which implies no significant parton energy loss in cold nuclear matter.
the single electron spectra measured in Run8 d+Au collisions at 200 GeV is not consistent with binary scaling of p+ p collisions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the single electron spectra for d+Au collisions are consistent with the results of p+p collisions.
we have measured the single electron spectra in d+Au at s N N=200 GeV and compared to the p+p results from the 2005 RHIC run (RHIC Run3).
the single electron spectra in d+Au and Au+Au are similar at the highest measured p T and the suppression in Au+Au is not due to cold nuclear matter effects.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the heavy flavor production in d+Au is suppressed at high p T compared to p+p collisions.
the single electron spectra are measured for d+Au collisions at 200 GeV and compared with the spectra from p+p collisions at the same energy and the results are compared with theoretical models.
the heavy flavor mesons are not suppressed in d+Au compared to p+p collisions.
